retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - preserve the referenced identity, body proportions, costume and ink-and-wash treatment while giving the same person a working pose. Use the face detail for identity and the full-body views for clothing structure; do not copy their neutral standing poses.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): partially_preserved - retain the hall and furnishing relationships in a closer oblique viewpoint. Only the working candlestick moves slightly within its original area; furnishings outside the crop need not be shown.

detailed_description:
The video retains the references' hand-painted ink-and-wash appearance: layered charcoal robe washes, broken brush edges and restrained warm-gray painted skin. Preserve the volume already expressed by the reference washes without replacing them with glossy three-dimensional shading or flattening the face into a few abstract lines.
[Shot 1] The camera starts close to the altar on the congregation side, slightly off the central aisle, looking obliquely toward <Subject 1> behind it. Frame him from head to waist, with his face, both hands and the working candlestick base comfortably visible. The altar top and hanging cloth occupy the lower foreground and naturally conceal the lower body. Use a near-eye-level viewpoint with a gentle downward angle for readable hand contact. Camera position and focal length remain fixed throughout.

The priest stands beside the candlestick on the right in <Picture 6>, shoulders relaxed and upper body inclined slightly toward the tabletop. His gaze stays lowered and his mouth remains closed. His anatomical right hand contacts the side of the candlestick base; his left hand rests separately on clear tabletop away from the brown book. From 0.00 to 1.00 seconds he holds this contact. From 1.00 to 3.50 seconds his right fingers and wrist make one slow, very small adjustment of the base within its original area, keeping the candlestick upright and supported on the altar. From 3.50 to 5.00 seconds he stops and holds still without withdrawing either hand. No walking, head turn, lifting or additional gesture.

Keep his facial proportions and short graying facial hair consistent with <Picture 4>, and maintain the restrained painted hand anatomy of <Picture 5> while adapting the fingers to the contact. The black robe retains layered matte ink shapes, broken edges and readable folds. The right-shoulder patch stays on the correct side and is visible only as the pose permits. Do not force back details into this front-oblique view.

Unify figure and hall through the same directional daylight and muted wash values. Light from the hall's physical left-side windows affects the priest, hands and altar coherently in the new viewpoint. Use overlap, perspective and contact shading expressed in washes to place him behind the altar; do not paste a portrait into the original wide view. No white paper rectangle, cutout halo, independent portrait lighting, oily skin or satin robe highlights. Preserve the references' painted volume rather than imposing photographic pores or smooth synthetic gradients.

The altar stays rigid, the cloth and book remain still, and hand-to-base contact remains continuous. Do not move or duplicate other furnishings to fit the crop. Facial features, fingers and candlestick retain stable shapes. Painted texture follows the moving hand and remains stable on stationary surfaces without crawling, flicker or exposure changes. No cuts, extra people or montage of the reference views. The entire clip is silent.
